problems.title: Vertex-centric cost
problems.statement: A graph with n = 10⁶ vertices and D = 1,000 levels (a long chain-like graph).

parts.prompt: Thread-visits with vertex-centric BFS (n per level)?
Atomics on the global queue counter, unprivatised?

problems.title: Degree imbalance
problems.statement: A frontier of 32 vertices in one warp: 31 have degree 3, one has degree 30,000.
problems.solution: 30,000 iterations at 3.13% efficiency: hubs need a warp or block, or edge-level balancing.

problems.title: Direction optimisation
problems.statement: A level's frontier has 40% of the vertices; the graph has average degree 16.

parts.prompt: Edges examined top-down (frontier edges), as a fraction of all edges?
Bottom-up checks unvisited vertices and stops at the first parent found. Typically…
options: far fewer edges when the frontier is large

problems.solution: Top-down examines 40% of all edges; bottom-up stops at the first frontier neighbour, often after 1–2 checks.

problems.title: Claiming vertices
problems.statement: Two threads discover the same unvisited vertex u at the same time.

options: exactly one gets −1 back and appends u

problems.solution: One CAS succeeds; the other sees d + 1 and skips. Every vertex enters the queue once.

problems.title: BFS levels
problems.solution: Vertex 5 is 5 steps either way; 7 is 3 steps via 9 (0→9→8→7); deepest level 5.

problems.title: Edge-level balancing
problems.statement: A frontier of 1,000 vertices with 1,000,000 total edges; 4,096 threads, each taking a contiguous range of edges.

parts.prompt: What tells each thread which vertex its edges belong to?
options: An exclusive scan of degrees plus a binary search

problems.solution: 245 edges each; an exclusive scan of the frontier's degrees plus a binary search gives each thread its vertex (co-rank again).

problems.title: Bandwidth bound
problems.statement: BFS over a graph with 10⁸ edges stored in CSR (4-byte column indices), each edge examined once.

parts.prompt: Time at 1 TB/s, in ms (colIdx only)?

problems.solution: 0.4 ms for the index stream alone; the random level[] checks (32-byte sectors per 4-byte access) usually cost more.

problems.title: Order

options: No: atomic appends happen in timing order; levels are deterministic, queue order isn't

problems.solution: Results (levels) are deterministic; the order of discovery within a level isn't.

problems.title: Kernel launches
problems.statement: Level-synchronous BFS on a graph with diameter 50, each level a launch costing 5 µs plus work.

parts.prompt: For a road network (diameter in thousands), the fix?
options: Persistent kernel with a device-side work queue (or CUDA Graphs)

problems.solution: 250 µs here; road networks have thousands of levels with tiny frontiers, so launch overhead dominates and persistent or graph-based execution is needed.
